conservation.help_by: Protect shoreline buffers; support mangrove restoration projects.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t clear mangrove roots for beach access or dump trash in lagoons.

life_info.eating: Photosynthesis; snorkel roots (pneumatophores) breathe air. Makes energy from sunlight (and sometimes from clear shallow water light).
life_info.mating: Spreads by spores, seeds, propagules, or creeping rhizomes depending on the species.
life_info.habitat: Higher intertidal mudflats behind red mangroves. Forms habitat structure that shelters fish, crabs, and invertebrates.

fun_facts: Leaves can excrete salt crystals you can taste.
Pneumatophores are the mangrove’s snorkels at low tide.

conservation.help_by: Give wildlife space; pick reef-safe sunscreen and careful finning.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t feed fish, chase animals, or pocket living souvenirs.

life_info.eating: Algae and coral rock scraped with fused teeth. Loud crunching you can sometimes hear underwater.
life_info.mating: Aggregates to spawn; colors flash during courtship.
life_info.habitat: Shallow reefs and rubble where algae grows thick. Often in loose schools sweeping a reef face.

fun_facts: Big blues look painted with one giant watercolor wash.
Their beak is many teeth fused into a chisel.

conservation.help_by: Give wildlife space; pick reef-safe sunscreen and careful finning.
conservation.caution_against: Don’t feed fish, chase animals, or pocket living souvenirs.

life_info.eating: Turf algae and film scraped from reef surfaces. Pecks and scrapes with a small beak-like mouth — a living reef janitor.
life_info.mating: Spawns in groups over the reef at dusk; eggs drift with the current.
life_info.habitat: Caribbean coral reefs and rocky shallows where algae coats the rock. Juveniles are bright yellow loners; adults may school or keep a cleaning circuit.

fun_facts: Kids know this look from cartoon reefs — the real fish prefers salad to adventure.
Those scalpels at the tail base are real: don’t grab a tang.
